hints: Focus on the type of reaction first, hot concentrated sulfuric acid with a tertiary alcohol means dehydration by elimination to form alkenes.
Draw the carbocation at C3 and spot the three different neighbouring carbon groups that can lose an H, from C2, from C4, and from the C3 methyl group.
For each resulting C=C, check if both ends have two different groups, as that gives a pair of E/Z stereoisomers to add to your total count.
walkthrough:
**Identify the reaction as dehydration**

This is elimination of water from an alcohol to give an alkene. The OH on C3 leaves to give a tertiary carbocation:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}^+(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
This carbocation is already tertiary, so no rearrangement to a more stable ion is needed.

**Find the three sites for H removal**

An H can be removed from any carbon next to $\text{C}^+$. Here that is C2 ($\text{CH}_2$), C4 ($\text{CH}_2$) and the methyl attached to C3 ($\text{CH}_3$). Each site gives a different structural alkene skeleton.

**Draw the three structural alkenes**

From C2: $\text{3-methylhex-2-ene}$, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. From C4: $\text{3-methylhex-3-ene}$, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. From the methyl: $\text{3-methylenehexane}$, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}(=\text{CH}_2)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$.

**Add E/Z stereoisomerism**

For 3-methylhex-2-ene, C2 has $\text{CH}_3$ and H, C3 has $\text{CH}_3$ and propyl, so E and Z forms exist, 2 isomers. For 3-methylhex-3-ene, C3 has methyl and ethyl, C4 has H and ethyl, so E and Z forms exist, 2 isomers. For the terminal alkene $\text{C}=\text{CH}_2$, one carbon has two H atoms, so no E/Z, 1 isomer.

options.A: 3 counts only the three structural skeletons and forgets stereoisomerism. Both internal alkenes can exist as E and Z forms, so this is an undercount.
options.B: 4 usually comes from spotting E/Z for only one of the internal alkenes. Both 3-methylhex-2-ene and 3-methylhex-3-ene meet the E/Z condition, so you need two pairs, not one.
options.C: 5 is correct: 2 stereoisomers of 3-methylhex-2-ene plus 2 stereoisomers of 3-methylhex-3-ene plus 1 terminal alkene from the methyl group gives 5 distinct C7H14 products.
options.D: 6 overcounts, often by giving E/Z to the terminal methylene alkene or by inventing a rearranged skeleton. The $\text{C}=\text{CH}_2$ alkene cannot show E/Z and no more stable carbocation rearrangement is available.
